faq.a: Selcuk is associated with the Turkish form سَلْجُوق, whose core sense is selcuk; seljuk (turkish tribal name).

faq.q: What is the origin of Selcuk?
faq.a: Selcuk is associated with Turkish. Selcuk is Turkish, the name of the Seljuk tribal founder. It is used as a male given name.
No — the underlying form is Turkish, not Arabic.
Selcuk can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Turkish-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Selcuk should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. Selçuk is a Turkish tribal name, not a Quranic Arabic form.

faq.a: Romanization variants include Selcuk, selcuk. Script forms are سلجوق, سَلْجُوق, सलजूक़.

faq.a: Documented usage records this form as male. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
